Local 0.72.0, not specific to flo2's hosted server","source":"art:dev-storyflow-feedback-2026-09-27","statement":"RUN AS THE SKILL on the dev_storyflow field report (art:dev-storyflow-feedback-2026-09-27), triaged 2026-09-28.

① OBSERVED, verbatim (2026-09-27 evening, flo2.io hosted, reflow2 0.72.0): "`add_verification` revise: `findings` without `status` is refused, although 'content fields are optional to revise'. The reason given (a finding belongs to a run) is sound, but on a revise the stored run already has a status. The call cost a round-trip to re-send a status that had not changed." Expected: findings replaced, stored status kept. NOT affected: a revise of `description` (or `name`, `method`) alone succeeds.

② PRECEDENT: searched the raw refusal words and "findings without status". Nothing records this refusal as a defect. The guard's origin is chg:the-owners-word-rides-the-same-call-as-the-status-it-signs (#440, 8d61d40, 2026-09-06), from dec:idea-should-a-constructor-accept-the-owners-word-in-one-call proposal ② ("the common case is 'I just ran it and here is what it found'"). That is a CREATE-time case; the ruling never discusses revise. #440's own rationale records the class: "the epoch hint moved to a shared pre-check because a fix placed in one handler recurred on its sibling within a day."

③ CANDIDATES. (a) The guard reads the request and never consults the stored node. (b) The refusal is deliberate on revise too: new findings may belong to a NEW run whose verdict must be restated, so this is intent, not a defect. (c) It is specific to flo2's hosted engine (a different code path or version). (d) The observation is wrong: the refusal was about `last_run_at`, which was also sent.

④ DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT: on a LOCAL 0.72.0 scratch store (this separates out (c)), create a check with status passing + last_run_at + findings, then revise with `findings` ONLY (this separates out (d)). Read the refusal text and the stored node. For (b): read the source comment and the ruling for any revise reasoning.

⑤ RESULT (reflow2-mcp 0.72.0, one-shot, scratch store): create {name, method test, level unit, status passing, last_run_at 2026-09-25, findings "31/35, 4 expected"} → stored as given. Revise {id, findings "…parity check proves it"} → REFUSED, -32602: "`add_verification`: `findings` and `last_run_at` describe a RUN, so they need `status` — the run's outcome — in the same call … Nothing was written." Stored node unchanged, status still "passing". Control: revise {id, description} → accepted, all else kept. So (c) is refuted (it reproduces locally, same version) and (d) is refuted (findings alone triggers it). Source (crates/reflow2-mcp/src/tools/assure.rs): `if req.status.is_none() && (req.findings.is_some() || req.last_run_at.is_some()) { return Err(…) }`. This runs after RequiredFields has fetched the stored node, and it never looks at it. The comment gives the premise: "storing them would assert a run whose verdict nobody stated". On a revise of a node holding `status: passing`, the verdict WAS stated, so the premise is false. That holds (a). (b) is NOT refuted, only weakened: nothing in the ruling or the comment considers a revise, so the refusal on revise is unargued rather than chosen. Whether findings changed on a revise should inherit the stored verdict (a text correction) or must restate it (a new run) is a real question, and it is carried in dec:idea-revise-notes-guards-and-defaults-read-the-merged-node. Unchanged in current source (git diff v0.72.0 HEAD).

⑥ CLASS: one of four ways a revise-capable handler computes from the call instead of the merged node (fact:root-cause-the-revise-contract-is-implemented-per-handler-and-guarded-by-instances-2026-09-28). This one is a GUARD. Neither the record_finding fix nor the undated-note fix would touch it.

⑦ WHAT A PINNING TEST WOULD ASSERT (not written): on a check with a stored status, add_verification {id, findings} either succeeds and keeps the stored status, or, if the owner rules that findings must restate the verdict, refuses with a message that NAMES the stored status. Either way the decision is made against the node, not the call. The create-time refusal (no stored status, findings without status) must still refuse, as the counterweight.

CHEAPEST HONEST INTERIM, if the rule stays: say the stored status in the refusal ("this check's last run is recorded as `passing`; re-send it with the findings, or use set_verification_status"), so the round trip is at least informed.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: the flo2.io server's own reply was not observed here; the local reproduction on the same version is taken to stand for it. Whether the owner wants findings-on-revise to inherit the verdict is a ruling, not a measurement.

REPORTER'S CONCLUSIONS: "refused, although 'content fields are optional to revise'" — CONFIRMED, and not hosted-specific. "The reason given … is sound, but on a revise the stored run already has a status" — CONFIRMED as stated: the guard's premise is false on such a revise.
